Integrating the geometric power series twice from zero produces x /[(n +1)(n + 2)]. What
n=0
is the interval of convergence of this new series?
(A) (−1, 1) (B) [−1, 1) (C) (−1, 1] (D) [−1, 1] (E) R

solution.text:
The radius remains 1. At both endpoints the absolute terms are 1/[(n + 1)(n + 2)], a conver-
gent telescoping series. Both endpoints are gained even though the original geometric series
diverges at each. Integration changes endpoint behavior without changing the radius.

question.text:
A power series for f centered at zero has radius exactly 2. After termwise differentiation and
′
substitution, the series for g(x) = f (3x + 1) is centered at which point and has what radius?
(A) −1/3, 2/3 (B) 1/3, 2/3 (C) −1, 2 (D) −1/3, 2 (E) −1/3, 6

solution.text:
Differentiation leaves radius 2. Writing 3x + 1 = 3(x + 1/3) makes the new center −1/3; the
condition |3x + 1| < 2 becomes |x + 1/3| < 2/3. The exact radius is therefore 2/3.
